A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TransPrune work, and all supplied pages are readable, including v1 Appendix A. However, v2 refers to supplementary configurations and analyses without including that material, limiting comparison of those portions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaVA benchmark experiments, pruning ablations, token-distribution analyses, and appendix visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds Qwen2.5-VL, video, CDPruner-combination, latency/memory, and layer-selection results.

M1.justification: The TTV computation, accumulation mechanism, instruction-guided attention, and combined pruning score remain unchanged in Equations 1–6. Applying TransPrune to additional models and CDPruner combinations does not introduce a documented algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual video-question-answering evaluation on TGIF and MSVD using Video-LLaVA (Table 6), substantially extending the previous image-based coverage. The original eight image benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds CDPruner and its FastV/PDrop combinations as comparators for CDPruner+TransPrune (Table 5). Conversely, FastV disappears from the standalone TTV comparison, although it remains elsewhere. Comparator membership in the original LLaVA and VisionZip comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation settings include Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Video-LLaVA with accuracy/score metrics, MME latency/memory measurements, and jointly varied pruning/accumulation schedules. Existing default layers and alpha remain unchanged. Figure 2 also changes its stated direction measure from one minus absolute cosine similarity to cosine similarity despite retaining identical graphics; this establishes a reporting revision, not a confirmed recomputation.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused five-schedule layer-selection sensitivity study (Table 9), beyond the existing early-versus-later accumulation comparison. The four original ablations retain their scores after renumbering. Standalone TTV analysis is narrowed, and v1 Appendix A's two visualization examples are absent from the supplied v2; further referenced supplementary analyses cannot be checked.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new latency and memory results likewise provide no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial result sets for Qwen2.5-VL, CDPruner combinations, video, layer selection, and practical efficiency. Examples include 47.5 TGIF and 70.3 MSVD accuracy at 6.1 TFLOPs (Table 6), and 111.4 ms latency with 14.82 GB memory (Table 8). TTV-only reporting loses several entries, including VQA-v2 71.5 and aggregate accuracy 95.5% from v1 Table 4.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–7 are unchanged. The FLOPs expression moves from Section 3.3 to Section 4.3. Added explanations of middle-layer behavior are qualitative interpretations, not new proofs or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The central training-free TTV-plus-IGA efficiency claim remains. v2 extends the prominently claimed architectural generality to Qwen2.5-VL, explicitly distinguishes the contribution from similarity-based approaches, and emphasizes middle-layer transitions in the conclusion. The abstract/introduction no longer claim standalone TTV performance comparable to attention-based methods such as FastV.

C2.justification: v1 attributes weak early-layer performance to low-level visual or positional information. v2 instead develops an instruction-driven global-to-local explanation, arguing that middle layers integrate global context and local details. It also acknowledges coupled pruning/accumulation choices. The TextVQA weakness and positional-bias interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v1 Table 5's explicit retention-ratio arrays and final token counts are unavailable in the supplied v2, which instead references supplementary material. The future code-release statement and repository URL also disappear, without establishing any actual repository availability change. Alpha, default layers, A100 40GB hardware, and FlashAttention disclosures remain.

R1.justification: The projector-pruning discussion replaces Recoverable Compression and HICom with DivPrune and CDPruner, adds GridPrune and other references, and expands positioning against similarity-based criteria. TopV and ShortV gain bibliographic citations even though both were already evaluated in v1. The basic within-LLM research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, introduction, related-work passages, and explanatory paragraphs; changes 'in-LLM' to 'within-LLM'; moves efficiency analysis into Section 4.3; and reorders ablation discussion. These are targeted revisions within the retained overall structure, with much method prose unchanged.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reorganized: five new tables appear, the TTV-only table becomes a compact comparison, the configuration table and appendix figures are absent, Figure 5 shrinks to one column, and ablation rows gain highlighting. Figures 1–5 retain their underlying graphics, although captions and placement change.

improvement.justification: Direct latency/memory measurements strengthen practical-efficiency evidence beyond v1's FLOP estimates, while Qwen2.5-VL and video evaluations better support generalization. These provide a limited net improvement. Missing retention settings and appendix material, reduced TTV-only reporting, and sparse measurement details temper the gains and reduce reproducibility; the original method and shared results remain unchanged.
